title: Ravencoin consensus safety profile, August 2026 incident baseline
description: Behaviour a Ravencoin Core release must demonstrate before this project treats it as safe to sit behind an Electrum server. A release is certified against a profile, never against a version number: a numerically newer release proves nothing until it passes this suite.

candidateSources.note: Allowlist of repositories a candidate may be discovered from. Being listed here grants a release the right to be TESTED, never the right to be TRUSTED. Both entries are treated identically.

identity.note: The certified identity key is repository plus commit. Version and tag are metadata only. Two repositories publishing the same version are two different candidates.

tests.description: The release tag resolves, through its tag object where annotated, to exactly the candidate commit being certified.
When the deployment pins a published binary artifact, its SHA-256 matches both the release metadata and the published checksum file.
The exact candidate commit builds, producing ravend and raven-cli. A moving branch is never substituted for the candidate.
A fresh mainnet datadir with no network access produces the canonical Ravencoin mainnet genesis hash, proving the chain parameters were not altered.
On regtest the candidate starts, connects blocks, keeps blocks equal to headers, and serves getblockchaininfo, getblockhash and getblockheader coherently.
Asset consensus is still present and functional: an asset can be issued and queried on regtest, and the asset database survives a restart.
txindex and assetindex build and answer, since ElectrumX depends on getrawtransaction and listaddressesbyasset. REST must serve rest/block/<hash>.bin, which is how ElectrumX reads blocks.
The candidate's own consensus, PoW, validation and asset unit tests pass in its build tree. A skipped or absent suite is not a pass.

Post-KAWPOW headers remain 120 bytes with the declared height at byte offset 76, and each real boundary fixture re-hashes to its known block hash under KAWPOW light verification. Scope is harness: this certifies that the enforcement rule and the real incident fixtures in this project are intact. Evidence about the candidate's own behaviour comes from the core-scope tests.

Every forged fixture whose declared nHeight disagrees with its chain height is rejected at the enforcement boundary, and a truncated header is rejected as well. Scope is harness: this certifies that the enforcement rule and the real incident fixtures in this project are intact. Evidence about the candidate's own behaviour comes from the core-scope tests.

The real valid headers at and after the enforcement boundary are still accepted, so the rule rejects forgeries without rejecting the honest chain. Scope is harness: this certifies that the enforcement rule and the real incident fixtures in this project are intact. Evidence about the candidate's own behaviour comes from the core-scope tests.
On a datadir holding mainnet history, the candidate reports the canonical hash at height 4487775.
The transfer_overflow consensus deployment is known to the candidate and reports its activation state on mainnet rather than being absent, which is how an unpatched generation behaves.
A chainstate rebuild from existing block files reaches the same tip hash, so block-index and chainstate recovery behaviour is intact.

Consensus-relevant source differences against the last certified baseline are summarised for human review. Supplemental evidence only; it never substitutes for the behavioural tests, and it never upgrades a result.

reviewRequiredTriggers.note: If a candidate changes any of these areas in a way this profile version cannot confidently certify, the result is REVIEW_REQUIRED, never KNOWN_SAFE.
areas: proof of work algorithm or KAWPOW verification
block index or chainstate storage semantics

promotion.note: Conditions for automatic promotion to KNOWN_SAFE. Every one is required; absence of evidence is never treated as evidence.
requires: all mandatory-when-artifact-pinned tests PASS when an artifact is pinned
no test result is SKIPPED, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR
certification report is produced and hashed
policy generation and signing both succeed

scopes.core: observes the candidate binaries or runs the candidate's own test suite
scopes.harness: verifies this project's enforcement rule and fixture integrity, not Core itself
scopes.provenance: checks release metadata and artifact digests
scopes.advisory: supplemental human-review evidence; never changes a result
